To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SMT-based method is faster than the SAT-based method and that the SMT method is more efficient for the weighted generic pipeline paradigm than for the weighted bit transmission problem.

(i) the SMT-based approach is more effective than the SAT-based approach in terms of the number of BMC iterations needed for a successful BMC proof; (ii) the SMTbased approach is more effective in terms of the BMC proof time; (iii) the SMT approach is more effective for the weighted bit transmission problem; (iv) the SAT-based approach is more efficient for the generic pipeline paradigm.

(a) the SMT-based algorithm is more efficient than the SAT-based algorithm for the same systems (the weighted bit transmission problem) and properties (the WELTLK property that expresses the fact that the system eventually stabilizes), and (b) the SMTbased algorithm is more efficient (for the same systems) for properties expressible by WELTLK formulas with more complex temporal and epistemic components.
